name: query
description: Read a value out of a JSON document with a jq program, and return it as the step's result. Use to pull one field out for a switch to compare, to narrow a large document before it reaches a prompt, or to count and filter without spending a model turn. The result is one value: wrap the program in [ ] to return a list.

data.description: The JSON document to read, usually a step's result: "{{ steps.fetch.text }}". Pass this or path, not both.

path.description: A JSON file to read instead, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside it. Pass this or data, not both.

query.description: A jq program. ".verdict" reads a field, ".items | length" counts, "[.checks[] | select(.state == \"failed\") | .name]" filters and collects. It must produce exactly one value; a program that emits a stream is refused, so wrap it in [ ] to return them as one array.

default.description: What to answer when the query matches nothing or reads a field that is not there. Without it that case fails, which is usually what you want: a missing field is a wrong assumption about the data. Set it when absence is a real case, e.g. default: "none" with a matching switch case.

output_schema.description: The one value the query produced. A string is printed as itself, without quotes, so a switch can compare it and a prompt can carry it. Anything else is printed as JSON, so the next step reads it as .json. A number or a boolean is both at once.

exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, or a parameter is missing or the wrong type)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (path resolves outside the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: malformed data (the data is not JSON)
exit_codes.6: refused (the query does not compile, failed on this document, or produced more than one value)
exit_codes.7: no result (the query matched nothing, or read a field that is not there, and no default was given)
